question: Does requiring two completed contraction-and-recovery waves with declining downside supply identify classic or partial VCP structures more faithfully than broad VCP candidates?
scope: Semantic representation only. The broad detector supplies the evaluation universe, but its selected legs, pivot, score, entry, exit and portfolio rules are not reused by the representation.

fixed_method.causality: All bars through the completed signal day may be used; any trade would occur no earlier than the next valid market open.
fixed_method.wave: A completed wave is a confirmed high-low-high sequence. The recovery high must regain at least half of the decline without exceeding the first high by more than 4 percent.
fixed_method.chain: Use the latest two adjacent completed waves sharing their middle high. The second wave must be shallower and its downside volume-weighted price pressure must be lower.
fixed_method.pivot_integrity: After the second recovery high, completed closes may not exceed that pivot by more than one recent median daily range before the signal bar.
fixed_method.right_edge: The last pre-signal close must be in the upper half of the final wave.
fixed_method.demand: The completed signal bar must close above the recovered pivot, in the upper half of its own range, on volume above the median of the preceding 20 completed bars.
fixed_method.supported: The wave chain, pivot integrity, right-edge and demand conditions all hold. No weighted score is used.

fresh_blind_packet.exclusions: All cases from the two earlier semantic packets are excluded.
fresh_blind_packet.selection: Ascending SHA-256 of symbol, signal date, scale, and sealed representation status; future outcomes are not part of selection.

stop_rule: If any semantic gate fails, stop this representation. Do not vary swing span, recovery fraction, pivot tolerance, volume baseline or acceptance gates on the same or exposed packets.
next_if_pass: Implement a separately named matrix-native v3 candidate and run one fixed time-split diagnostic against forward-v2.
next_if_fail: Keep forward-v2 as the usable baseline and replace the representation concept rather than tuning this one.
